notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — no correctness bugs found in RFC 5280 §6.1 path validation logic. P1 risks are documentation/API surface issues: revocation coverage gap, misleading crate description, stub ambiguity, implementation limits.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — no unsafe code (forbid attribute enforced), no unwrap in production paths, non_exhaustive on all error enums, Display + source() on all errors, From impls for operator? chaining. Two minor clippy-level items filed (for→find/and_then, is_some_and). No ownership, lifetime, or type-design issues found.
Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: (1) RSA NULL-vs-absent params behavior depends on x509-cert PartialEq impl which I haven't verified against real-world certs; (2) pkix-chain-simple critical EKU behavior — the crate IS documented as strict/opinionated, this may be intentional and the doc description is the only thing that needs fixing. Uncertainty driven by: no test run performed, no real-world cert corpus tested. Would raise confidence if: cargo test --all-features passes, and at least one real CA-issued TLS cert is run through verify_simple to confirm the critical EKU behavior.
